node.title: Re^2: Variable-Width Lookbehind (hacked via recursion)
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Excellent point, thank you for spotting that! I can confirm that the (?= ) around (? ) can be removed in all cases in the root node (since (?<= ) is already zero-width). Makes the regexes even shorter! :-)

It's probably a vestige from the negative case like [id://1201959|here] or in the following, where the (?! (? ... ) ) is needed*.

# Match any /\d./ that is *not* preceded by an /a/ my $re5 = qr{ (?! (? (?<= a | (?=(?&lookback)) . ) ) ) (? \d . ) }msx; my $re5_short = qr /(?!((?<= a |(?=(?-1)).))) (\d.) /sx; for my $regex ($re5,$re5_short) { unlike "fo", $regex; unlike "x5", $regex; unlike "ab5 x4", $regex; like "5ab", $regex; like "x5 ab5", $regex; like "x5 ab5 x2", $regex; my @results; while ("x2 4x3a55aaa1" =~ /$regex/g) { push @results, $+{target} // $2 } is_deeply \@results, ["2 ","4x","3a"]; }

* Update: Hmm, actually, it turns out this seems to work too... (although putting the exact explanation of why into words is eluding me at the moment...)
